status_summary: The field-office shift and legal-office downsizing are partly underway, but no change to the FBI's reporting line, to its separate congressional affairs office, or to the Director's term was found. Director Kash Patel told Senate appropriators on 2026-05-12 that 604 special agents had been realigned from the National Capital Region to field offices since January 2025; his 2025-05-07 House statement had cited more than 1,000 positions moving out of Washington. The FBI and GSA announced on 2025-07-01 that the Ronald Reagan Building would become FBI headquarters, and Patel said in December 2025 that the Hoover Building would close. Bloomberg Law reported on 2026-08-04, citing unnamed sources, that Patel planned to shrink the Office of General Counsel, which the Mandate puts at about 300 attorneys. As of 2026-10-07 the FBI's leadership page still lists the Office of General Counsel and the Office of Congressional Affairs under the Director; it does not list an Office of Public Affairs but does list an Office of Engagement, and no source reviewed says any of the three offices was eliminated.

timeline.event: Patel's written statement to the House Appropriations CJS subcommittee says more than 1,000 positions are moving out of Washington, D.C., to field locations and describes realigning the organizational structure; it does not mention the general counsel's office.
FBI and GSA announce the Ronald Reagan Building complex will become the FBI headquarters, replacing earlier plans for a new suburban campus; the release gives no timeline or staffing numbers.
Patel announces on X that the Hoover Building will close permanently and most headquarters staff will move to the Reagan Building (December 2025; exact day not confirmed, first of month used).

Patel's statement to the Senate Appropriations CJS subcommittee on the FY2027 budget says the FBI has realigned 604 special agents from the National Capital Region to field offices since January 2025; it does not discuss office consolidation or reporting lines.

Bloomberg Law reports, citing unnamed sources, that Patel plans to cut the FBI Office of General Counsel (several hundred lawyers) and that the office has been pushing staff toward early retirement and has considered terminations.

title: Restructure FBI: reporting line, legal and press offices, smaller headquarters
uncertainties: The Bloomberg Law article is paywalled and only an excerpt was readable; the general counsel cut rests on unnamed sources and an FBI spokesman is quoted as denying related tension. The FBI leadership page is a snapshot of listed offices and may not be exhaustive, so its omission of a public affairs office does not show that office was eliminated. A Cornell LII copy of 28 CFR 0.15 (source note from 1981, currency date not shown) does not name the FBI among the Deputy Attorney General's units and shows no supervision by the Criminal or National Security Division, but the eCFR could not be fetched (robots restriction), so a recent amendment is not ruled out; the DOJ organization chart page shows no reporting lines. Patel's 2026-09-15 Senate Judiciary oversight statement did not address the restructuring. Field-move figures differ across sources (more than 1,000 positions in 2025, 604 special agents in 2026, and a 2026 social-media figure above 1,500 relayed by a commentary site that was dropped as a source). The Hoover closure date is a placeholder. Searches run: FBI Office of General Counsel cuts; bill to end the ten-year term (nothing found); Patel's current status (returned only prediction-market pages); Federal Register search of DOJ rules mentioning the FBI (no reporting-line change).
